cards.front: Which delimiters does a char literal use?
cards.extra: A character literal is a character or an escape sequence enclosed in single quotes. The literal is always of type char, never String, so 'a' and "a" are values of two unrelated types.
cards.example: char c = 'a';   // ASCII single quotes, exactly one character

cards.front: How many characters may sit between the quotes of a char literal?
cards.back: Exactly one — '' and 'ab' are both compile errors
cards.extra: The JLS makes it an error for anything other than the closing quote to follow the single character, so the pair must enclose one character or one escape such as '\n'. An empty literal has no character left to store.
cards.example:
char ok = 'a';
// char bad = '';     // error: empty character literal
// char bad2 = 'ab';  // error: too many characters in character literal

cards.front: Is an empty string literal "" legal?
cards.back: Yes — it is a String of length 0
cards.extra: A string literal consists of zero or more characters enclosed in double quotes, so "" is a real object with length() == 0. The char form '' has no zero-length case and does not compile.
